prompt:
Our certificate bootstrap job needs a small, dependency-free SDDC Manager client that can be run again after an uncertain result without installing the same trusted certificate twice. Implement the single source file `SddcTrustedCertificatesClient.java` and preserve its existing public API.

Before implementing, research the `getTrustedCertificates` and `addTrustedCertificate` operations in the SDDC Manager OpenAPI specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository and cite the specification URLs consulted.

Required public API:

- `SddcTrustedCertificatesClient(URI baseUri, String bearerToken, HttpClient httpClient)` uses the injected JDK HTTP client and bearer token.
- `List<TrustedCertificate> listTrustedCertificates()` calls `getTrustedCertificates`. Return an immutable list sorted by alias ascending, with certificate text as the deterministic tie-breaker. Response order is not stable.
- `List<TrustedCertificate> ensureTrustedCertificate(String pemCertificate)` implements a retry-safe ensure-present mutation. Read first and skip the mutation when that exact certificate is already present. Otherwise call `addTrustedCertificate` with JSON containing the required `certificate` property and no deprecated optional property. A successful collection response must also be sorted before it is returned.
- If add returns the documented duplicate status, perform one fresh collection read and succeed only if the exact certificate is now present. If the POST has an uncertain I/O outcome, likewise reconcile with one GET; never blindly repeat the POST. A later call with the same PEM must not duplicate the effect.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Accept: application/json` on every request, and the documented media type on the mutation. Treat only documented success statuses as success. Surface other statuses and malformed responses as `IOException` without putting the bearer token or certificate text in the message.
- Keep `TrustedCertificate` as the public nested record declared by the starter. Use only the Java standard library and keep all client implementation in this one source file.

Do not modify `TestMain.java` or `verify.sh`. Run `bash verify.sh` until it prints `all checks passed`.
